content: The following are descriptions of various medical conditions and classifications related to perinatal and congenital disorders, as well as birth injuries, based on the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10): 1. Congenital Anemia: Congenital anemia due to fetal blood loss (P61.3). Other congenital anemias not classified elsewhere, including unspecified congenital anemia (P61.4). Other specified perinatal hematological disorders (P61.8). Unspecified perinatal hematological disorders (P61.9). 2. Renal and Perinatal Conditions: Congenital renal failure, including uremia in newborns (P96.0). Termination of pregnancy affecting the fetus or newborn (P96.4). Complications from intrauterine procedures not classified elsewhere (P96.5). Other specified conditions originating in the perinatal period (P96.8). Unspecified conditions originating in the perinatal period, including congenital debility (P96.9). 3. Fetal Growth Disorders: Slow fetal growth and fetal malnutrition (P05). Infants light for gestational age, typically with weight below the 10th percentile but length above the 10th percentile (P05.0). Infants small for gestational age, with both weight and length below the 10th percentile (P05.1). Fetal malnutrition without being light or small for gestational age, often presenting with dry, peeling skin and loss of subcutaneous tissue (P05.2). Unspecified slow fetal growth or fetal growth retardation (P05.9). 4. Gestational and Birth Weight Disorders: Extremely low birth weight, defined as 999 grams or less (P07.0). Other low birth weights, ranging from 1,000 to 2,499 grams (P07.1). Extreme immaturity, defined as less than 28 completed weeks of gestation (P07.2). Other preterm infants, between 28 and 37 completed weeks of gestation (P07.3). Disorders related to long gestation and high birth weight, including exceptionally large babies (4,500 grams or more) (P08.0) and other heavy-for-gestational-age infants (P08.1). Post-term infants with a gestation period of 42 weeks or more but not heavy for gestational age (P08.2). 5. Birth Trauma: Intracranial lacerations and hemorrhages due to birth injury, including subdural hemorrhage (P10.0), cerebral hemorrhage (P10.1), intraventricular hemorrhage (P10.2), subarachnoid hemorrhage (P10.3), tentorial tears (P10.4), and other or unspecified intracranial injuries (P10.8, P10.9). Other birth injuries to the central nervous system, such as cerebral edema (P11.0), brain damage (P11.1, P11.2), facial nerve injury (P11.3), cranial nerve injuries (P11.4), and spinal cord injuries (P11.5). Birth injuries to the scalp, including cephalhematoma (P12.0), chignon (P12.1), subaponeurotic hemorrhage (P12.2), bruising (P12.3), and injuries from monitoring devices (P12.4). Birth injuries to the skeleton, such as skull fractures (P13.0), femur injuries (P13.2), and clavicle fractures (P13.4). Birth injuries to the peripheral nervous system, including Erb paralysis (P14.0), Klumpke paralysis (P14.1), and phrenic nerve paralysis (P14.2). 6. Intrapartum Complications: Intrauterine hypoxia, including cases first noted during labor and delivery (P20.1) or unspecified (P20.9). Birth asphyxia, excluding low Apgar scores without mention of asphyxia or respiratory problems (P21). 7. Congenital Malformations: Malformations of the heart, including cardiac chambers (Q20), septa (Q21), valves (Q22, Q23), and great arteries or veins (Q25, Q26). Malformations of the respiratory system, such as the nose (Q30), larynx (Q31), trachea (Q32), and lungs (Q33). Malformations of the digestive system, including the esophagus (Q39), intestines (Q41, Q42), and gallbladder or liver (Q44). Musculoskeletal malformations, such as polydactyly (Q69), syndactyly (Q70), and limb reduction defects (Q71–Q73). 8. Other Congenital Conditions: Congenital ichthyosis (Q80), epidermolysis bullosa (Q81), and other skin malformations (Q82). Congenital malformation syndromes due to known exogenous causes (Q86) or affecting multiple systems (Q87). Down syndrome (Q90). 9. Neonatal Muscle Tone Disorders: Transient neonatal myasthenia gravis (P94.0). Congenital hypertonia (P94.1) and hypotonia (P94.2), including nonspecific floppy baby syndrome. Other or unspecified disorders of muscle tone in newborns (P94.8, P94.9). 10. Placental and Cord Abnormalities: Conditions such as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome caused by placental or cord abnormalities (P02.3). This detailed classification system is used to document and analyze perinatal and congenital conditions, as well as birth-related injuries, to improve understanding and care for affected individuals.
